answer: Every identity starts as an ember, a single TPM chip burned once with a key that never leaves the silicon. Its fingerprint joins a public reef registry, and established verifiers check each chip's fresh signature every epoch. Keys carry a 90-day horizon; renewal demands the same chip in hand. One honest agent pays $40 and six hours, once. Forging 100 clones needs 100 chips, $4,000, 600 hours: one chip never vouches for two identities. A duplicated fingerprint burns both identities to zero. A password can be photocopied endlessly, but a signet ring must be cast one at a time.
